In src/click/core.py I touch: the Context docstring (new :param validate_nesting: + versionchanged), Context.__init__ (one new kwarg at the END of the signature, plus two attributes after self._exit_stack), Context.__exit__, Context.close, Context._make_sub_context, Command.invoke's sub-context setup in Context.invoke, and Group.to_info_dict; in shell_completion.py only _resolve_context. If your snapshot/restore adds methods, please put them after Context.get_help or before Context.meta rather than inside __init__/close, and do not edit CHANGES.rst (I will not either) so we do not conflict. Which parts of core.py do you touch?

agent2: thanks, agreed on the layout. My branch claude/7 is pushed and its draft PR is open. New Context attributes: validate_nesting (plain bool, fine to snapshot) and _child_contexts (set of live child Context objects, a live guard like _depth/_exit_stack). Please EXCLUDE _child_contexts from save_state/restore_state: deep-copying it would copy child contexts (each links back to its parent), and restoring a stale copy would resurrect closed children, so a later close() with validate_nesting=True would wrongly raise RuntimeError. Everything else I add is in close()/__exit__/_make_sub_context/invoke/Group.to_info_dict, none of it new state. I will mark ready shortly; if you land first I will merge main, if I land first please merge team/main.
